A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TokenSkip research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained experiments across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSM8K and MATH-500 experiments, including accuracy, token counts, latency, compression analyses, and CoT recovery examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds prompt-baseline results, a token-importance distribution analysis, and out-of-domain evaluation.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains importance-based token pruning, filtered self-generated CoTs, ratio-conditioned fine-tuning, and autoregressive inference. Section 3 makes mixed-ratio training more explicit, but v1 already specifies the same compression-ratio sampling in Sections 4.1 and B.1.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds MMLU-STEM, extending evaluation beyond the original two mathematical reasoning benchmarks to diverse STEM subjects. It also evaluates transfer from MATH training to GSM8K, alongside the retained in-domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 broadens the actual comparison by adding BeConcise, OnlyNumbers, and AbbreWords on both benchmarks. Prompt is retained under the name LC-Prompt, and Truncation remains. The compressor comparison removes GPT-4o-Optimal while retaining GPT-4o, LLMLingua-2, and Selective Context.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols evaluate a MATH-trained LLaMA model on other benchmarks and compare Qwen2.5-14B outputs at ratios 1.0 and 0.7 to identify skipped and retained tokens. Existing training settings, metrics, greedy decoding, and length budgets remain unchanged; several disclosures move to Appendix B.1.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative evidence about whether generated CoTs discard low-importance tokens in Figure 7 and tests cross-domain robustness in Appendix B.4. These address mechanism and generalization beyond v1's analyses. The GPT-4o-Optimal flexible-compression experiment is removed; other compression-ratio and length-budget analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new token-importance density plot characterizes token scores rather than uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline scores, token-distribution findings, and transfer results. For example, Table 4 reports MMLU-STEM accuracy of 58.1% with 188.87 tokens at ratio 0.5, versus the original model's 58.5% and 356.31 tokens. GPT-4o-Optimal results disappear. Retained Table 1 and Table 2 numerical entries are unchanged; Table 4's MATH-500 block repeats existing results.

T1.justification: Equation 3 replaces np.percentile notation with Qγ while restating the same verbally specified percentile-threshold rule. The retention inequality and training and decoding equations remain substantively unchanged. No theoretical propositions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same importance-based compression contribution, novelty claim, and headline Qwen2.5-14B result. The added experiments support the existing contribution without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations supporting cross-domain generalizability and selective removal of low-importance tokens. It describes GPT-4o as an upper bound and removes the GPT-4o-Optimal interpretation motivating flexible compression ratios. The stated limitations concerning larger models, long CoTs, and the compressor's training domain remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 supplies exact prompts for the newly evaluated baselines. Instructions involving the GPT-4o-Optimal variant and its special inference token are removed with that experiment. Existing hardware, optimization settings, software, and code/checkpoint access disclosures are retained, with some consolidated in Appendix B.1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lee et al. (2025) for prompt baselines and the MMLU reference by Hendrycks et al. (2021a). It removes discussion and citations for Hu et al. (2023), Mu et al. (2024), and Wingate et al. (2022). The central positioning around importance-based pruning using a small model remains.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of Section 3, experimental setup, and related work, plus author-order and affiliation-marker changes. Implementation material is consolidated in the appendix, which gains Sections B.3 and B.4. The overall narrative and main section order remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 7 and Tables 3–4, expands Table 1, and removes the GPT-4o-Optimal point and legend entry from the renumbered compressor plot. Figure 4's caption changes while its artwork remains; other displays are relocated or resized within the retained two-column layout.

improvement.justification: Additional prompt comparisons, the token-importance diagnostic, and cross-domain evaluation provide useful evidence about competitiveness, mechanism, and transferability that v1 lacked. Removing GPT-4o-Optimal narrows the exploration of flexible compression, and statistical uncertainty remains unreported. Overall, the additions modestly strengthen the paper without fundamentally changing its contribution or evidential foundation.
